flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 2 attach to extent of application?
flashcards.back: Continuous
flashcards.expl: Applies to Union civil services and posts. Eleven exclusions, clauses (a) to (k): Railways, casual/daily-rated/part-time, contingency-paid, industrial workmen, work-charged, All India Services, locally recruited overseas staff, contract staff (unless the contract provides otherwise), persons covered
flashcards.src: Rule 2, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 3 attach to definitions (13 clauses, a to m)?
flashcards.back: Date of retirement: afternoon of the last day of the month
flashcards.expl: Thirteen definitions, clauses (a) to (m). The examinable ones are (a) Administrator, (b) Audit Officer, (c) authority competent to grant leave (First Schedule), (d) completed years of service — which expressly includes leave, including EOL, and (e) date of retirement — the afternoon of the last day
flashcards.src: Rule 3, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: Date of retirement: afternoon of the las

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 4 attach to government servants on temporary transfer or foreign service?
flashcards.back: EL 120 days at a time with a foreign employer
flashcards.expl: The rules follow the servant on temporary transfer to Railways, a State Government or foreign service within India. Out of India, or on transfer to the Armed Forces, they apply only so far as the terms provide. A servant on foreign service with a foreign employer may be granted earned leave of not m
flashcards.src: Rule 4, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: EL 120 days at a time with a foreign emp

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 5 attach to transfer from services or posts governed by other leave rules?
flashcards.back: Carried forward within the Rule 26 ceiling
flashcards.expl: Leave already running under another rule-set is completed under that rule-set. The balance at credit is carried forward only so far as Rule 26 allows, and carried-forward leave is exhausted first.
flashcards.src: Rule 5, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: Carried forward within the Rule 26 ceili

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 6 attach to transfer to an industrial establishment?
flashcards.back: Suo motu on the date of transfer
flashcards.expl: On transfer to an industrial establishment outside these rules, the leave balance is cashed out suo motu, EL and HPL together, capped at 300 days.
flashcards.src: Rule 6, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: Suo motu on the date of transfer

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 7 attach to right to leave?
flashcards.back: No time limit — discretionary
flashcards.expl: Leave is not a matter of right: it may be refused or revoked. The kind of leave cannot be changed to the servant's disadvantage except on his own written request. Even a refusal should be by written order.
flashcards.src: Rule 7, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 8 attach to regulation of claim to leave?
flashcards.back: Rules as in force on the date of application and grant
flashcards.expl: The claim is regulated by the rules in force when leave is applied for and granted, not by the rules in force when the leave was earned. This is the classic 240/300 amendment trap.
flashcards.src: Rule 8, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: Rules as in force on the date of applica

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 9 attach to dismissal, removal and resignation?
flashcards.back: Lapse takes effect from the date of dismissal, removal or resignation
flashcards.expl: Leave lapses from the date of dismissal, removal or resignation, and no cash equivalent is payable. Exceptions: Rule 39, reinstatement, and a technical resignation through the proper channel.
flashcards.src: Rule 9, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: Lapse takes effect from the date of dism

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 10 attach to commutation of one kind of leave into another?
flashcards.back: 30 days from rejoining duty
flashcards.expl: One kind of leave may be commuted into another on a request made within 30 days of rejoining; the concession is discretionary and any excess salary is adjusted.
flashcards.src: Rule 10, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 12 attach to maximum continuous leave?
flashcards.back: 5 years continuous
flashcards.expl: Five years is the outer limit of continuous leave; beyond it the servant is deemed to have resigned. Only the President may extend it, on exceptional circumstances.
flashcards.src: Rule 12, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 13 attach to service or employment while on leave?
flashcards.back: Previous sanction — before the employment begins
flashcards.expl: Previous sanction is required for any service or employment during leave. Outside India the sanction is the President's; within India, the appointing authority's. Cancelled LPR is encashable under Rule 39(2) — Rule 13(3)(a)-(b) survive, clauses (c)-(d) are deleted.
flashcards.src: Rule 13, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 14 attach to application for leave?
flashcards.back: Apply before the leave is to commence; extension before expiry
flashcards.expl: Leave is applied for in Form 1, and an extension of leave goes in the same Form 1. Where the servant cannot sign, the application may be signed by the persons listed in the rule.
flashcards.src: Rule 14, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: Apply before the leave is to commence; e

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 15 attach to leave account?
flashcards.back: Continuous maintenance
flashcards.expl: One account per servant, in Form 2. Who keeps it depends on how the pay is drawn: Audit Officer for Gazetted officers paid through the PAO, Head of Office for Gazetted officers paid directly, Head of Office for all non-Gazetted staff.
flashcards.src: Rule 15, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 16 attach to verification of title to leave?
flashcards.back: Provisional sanction 60 days (GSR No. 1422, 21.11.1979)
flashcards.expl: Admissibility is verified first. Where that is not possible, provisional sanction is limited to 60 days and is open to later modification.
flashcards.src: Rule 16, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 17 attach to leave not granted in certain circumstances?
flashcards.back: From the date of the competent authority's decision
flashcards.expl: Once the punishing authority has decided on dismissal, removal or compulsory retirement, leave cannot be granted. This is a bar, not a discretion.
flashcards.src: Rule 17, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: From the date of the competent authority

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 19 attach to leave on medical certificate?
flashcards.back: Waiver up to 3 days at a time
flashcards.expl: Medical-certificate leave runs on Form 3 (Gazetted), Form 4 (non-Gazetted), Form 3-A (disability) and Form 5 (fitness to return). The certificate may be waived up to 3 days at a time — and that leave is then not treated as leave on medical certificate.
flashcards.src: Rule 19, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: Waiver up to 3 days at a time

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 20 attach to government servant unlikely to be fit to return to duty?
flashcards.back: 12 months at a time; 6 months where permanently incapacitated
flashcards.expl: Where recovery is uncertain, leave up to 12 months at a time, extended on fresh certificates. Where the servant is permanently incapacitated and already on leave, the cap is 6 months.
flashcards.src: Rule 20, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: 12 months at a time; 6 months where perm

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 21 attach to commencement and termination of leave?
flashcards.back: Charge handover / resumption dates
flashcards.expl: Leave begins on the day the charge is handed over and ends the day before the charge is resumed. A holiday in between does not shift either end-date.
flashcards.src: Rule 21, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 23 attach to recall to duty?
flashcards.back: Recall may issue before the leave expires
flashcards.expl: Sub-rules (1) and (2) are deleted; sub-rule (3) survives. Recall is compulsory in every case, and the servant draws TA and leave salary until he joins.
flashcards.src: Rule 23, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: Recall may issue before the leave expire

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 24 attach to return from leave?
flashcards.back: Before resuming duty
flashcards.expl: Permission is needed to return. LPR needs the appointing authority's consent. Medical-certificate leave requires a Form 5 fitness certificate on return.
flashcards.src: Rule 24, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 25 attach to absence after expiry of leave?
flashcards.back: From the day after expiry of sanctioned leave
flashcards.expl: Overstay is debited as HPL to the extent of the balance, then as EOL. No leave salary at all for the overstay, and wilful absence invites CCA action.
flashcards.src: Rule 25, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: From the day after expiry of sanctioned

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 26 attach to earned leave?
flashcards.back: Credited 1 January and 1 July; 180 days at a time in India
flashcards.expl: Earned leave: 15 days credited in advance on 1 January and 1 July (30 days a year); accumulation ceiling 300 days; 285-day buffer under which the next credit is held apart; 180 days at a time in India, 150 for the Exception category, 300 if spent abroad in the specified countries.
flashcards.src: Rule 26, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 27 attach to calculation of earned leave?
flashcards.back: Applied at the next half-year credit; exit credit up to the relevant date
flashcards.expl: The pro-rata engine. Credit is 2 1/2 days per completed month, applied in the joining half-year and the exit cases: retirement or resignation up to the date; removal or dismissal only up to the end of the preceding month; death up to the date of death. EOL and dies non cost 1/10th of the period, cap
flashcards.src: Rule 27, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: Applied at the next half-year credit; ex

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 28 attach to earned leave in vacation departments?
flashcards.back: Half-yearly 5 days; year = 12 months of actual duty
flashcards.expl: Vacation departments start from a 5 + 5 = 10 day base, and add a proportionate share of 20 days for vacation not taken, up to 30 days a year. No vacation at all in a year means Rule 26 applies. The 300-day ceiling is unchanged.
flashcards.src: Rule 28, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 29 attach to half pay leave?
flashcards.back: Credited 1 January and 1 July
flashcards.expl: Half pay leave: 10 days credited per half-year (20 a year), earned at 5/3 days per completed month, with no accumulation ceiling. Dies non costs 1/18th of the period, capped at 10 days. It may be taken on medical grounds or private affairs.
flashcards.src: Rule 29, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 30 attach to commuted leave?
flashcards.back: Study commutation 180 days in the entire service
flashcards.expl: One day of commuted leave buys full pay at the price of two days of half pay leave. It needs a medical certificate, and satisfaction that the servant will return. Study commutation up to 180 days is the certificate-free route. Non-return triggers recovery of the difference unless the retirement is o
flashcards.src: Rule 30, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: Study commutation 180 days in the entire

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 31 attach to leave not due?
flashcards.back: Half pay leave likely to be earned later; 360 days in all under sub-rule (1-A)
flashcards.expl: Leave not due is HPL advanced against future earnings, capped at 360 days in the entire service, on medical certificate, for permanent and quasi-permanent staff. Temporary staff get the same 360 days only for TB, leprosy, cancer or mental illness. It is not available for leave preparatory to retirem
flashcards.src: Rule 31, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: Half pay leave likely to be earned later

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 32 attach to extraordinary leave?
flashcards.back: 3 / 6 / 18 / 24 months, according to service and circumstances
flashcards.expl: EOL carries no leave salary. The sub-rule (2) ladder is 3 months general, 6 months with one year's service plus a medical certificate, 18 months for the specified diseases, and 24 months for study in the public interest with three years' service. Study EOL beyond the limits needs a Form 6 bond.
flashcards.src: Rule 32, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 33 attach to leave to probationers and apprentices?
flashcards.back: Probation period; apprentice one month a year
flashcards.expl: A probationer cannot be carried on leave beyond the probation period, except on EOL. An apprentice gets one month of medical-certificate leave on half pay a year, plus EOL.
flashcards.src: Rule 33, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: Probation period; apprentice one month a

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 34 attach to re-employment and counting of past service?
flashcards.back: At the time of re-employment
flashcards.expl: Past service counts for leave wherever it counts for pension; the leave account follows the pension counting rather than a separate test.
flashcards.src: Rule 34, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 38 attach to leave preparatory to retirement?
flashcards.back: Up to the date of retirement
flashcards.expl: LPR is the whole balance taken at the end: EL up to 300 days plus HPL, up to the date of retirement. EOL is expressly outside LPR. Where LPR is cancelled under Rule 13(3)(b), it is encashable under Rule 39(2).
flashcards.src: Rule 38, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: Up to the date of retirement

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 38A attach to earned leave encashment with LTC?
flashcards.back: Per LTC occasion; 60 days per career
flashcards.expl: LTC encashment: 10 days per occasion, 60 days in the career, and at least 30 days of EL must remain after encashment. If the LTC is not availed, the money comes back with interest at 2% above the PF rate.
flashcards.src: Rule 38A, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: Per LTC occasion; 60 days per career

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 39 attach to cash in lieu of leave on retirement?
flashcards.back: Suo motu on the date of retirement
flashcards.expl: On retirement the authority acts suo motu: EL and HPL are both encashed, together capped at 300 days, on the retirement-date pay plus DA. HPL cannot be commuted to top up an EL shortfall. Nothing is paid on resignation, dismissal or removal — that is Rule 9.
flashcards.src: Rule 39, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: Suo motu on the date of retirement

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 39A attach to cash equivalent on death in service?
flashcards.back: Date immediately following death is the calculation date
flashcards.expl: Death in service: the family gets cash equivalent of up to 300 days, computed as if the servant had gone on earned leave on the day after death. LTC encashment already taken is subtracted from the 300-day ceiling, and there is no DCRG set-off.
flashcards.src: Rule 39A, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: Date immediately following death is the

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 39B attach to cash equivalent on invalidation?
flashcards.back: Date of invalidation
flashcards.expl: Invalidation on permanent incapacity: EL and HPL both encashed, 300-day cap, suo motu. A non-permanent or non-quasi-permanent servant gets EL only — no HPL.
flashcards.src: Rule 39B, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 39C attach to order of payment of cash equivalent?
flashcards.back: At the time of payment
flashcards.expl: The succession ladder for money not yet received: widow or husband, son, unmarried daughter, widowed daughter, father, mother, married daughter, minor brother, unmarried sister, widowed sister, then the eldest child of the eldest predeceased son.
flashcards.src: Rule 39C, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 39D attach to cash equivalent on permanent absorption in a PSU?
flashcards.back: Date of absorption
flashcards.expl: PSU absorption: earned leave only, up to 300 days, suo motu. HPL is not encashed. The body must be wholly or substantially owned or controlled by the Central or a State Government.
flashcards.src: Rule 39D, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 40 attach to leave salary?
flashcards.back: Paid monthly
flashcards.expl: The master rate card: EL full pay, HPL and LND half pay, commuted leave full pay, EOL nothing. DA follows; HRA applies on the stated conditions.
flashcards.src: Rule 40, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 41 attach to drawal of leave salary?
flashcards.back: Monthly drawal
flashcards.expl: Leave salary is drawn in rupees, in India — even where the servant is on leave abroad.
flashcards.src: Rule 41, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 42 attach to advance of leave salary?
flashcards.back: Leave of at least 30 days
flashcards.expl: Advance of leave salary: leave of at least 30 days, advance up to one month's pay and allowances computed on the leave salary admissible, less statutory deductions.
flashcards.src: Rule 42, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 43 attach to maternity leave?
flashcards.back: 180 days; 45 days for miscarriage/abortion
flashcards.expl: Maternity leave: 180 days on full pay for a female servant with fewer than two surviving children; 45 days for miscarriage or abortion, irrespective of the number of children. It is not debited to the leave account, may be combined with any leave, and due leave up to two years may follow it.
flashcards.src: Rule 43, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 43A attach to paternity leave?
flashcards.back: Window: 15 days before delivery to 6 months after
flashcards.expl: Paternity leave: 15 days for a male servant with fewer than two surviving children, availed within the window from 15 days before delivery to six months after it. The leave lapses if not taken in that window.
flashcards.src: Rule 43A, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: Window: 15 days before delivery to 6 mon

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 43AA attach to paternity leave on adoption?
flashcards.back: Within 6 months of adoption
flashcards.expl: Paternity leave on adoption: 15 days, on a valid adoption of a child below one year, availed within six months of the adoption.
flashcards.src: Rule 43AA, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 43B attach to child adoption leave?
flashcards.back: 180 days from the date of adoption
flashcards.expl: Child adoption leave: 180 days for a female servant with fewer than two surviving children, on a valid adoption of a child below one year. Not debited to the account.
flashcards.src: Rule 43B, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: 180 days from the date of adoption

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 43C attach to child care leave?
flashcards.back: 730 days in the entire service; 120 days a spell
flashcards.expl: Child care leave: 730 days in the entire service for the two eldest surviving children, at 100% pay for the first 365 days and 80% for the next 365. Spells: 3 a year normally, 6 for a single female parent, minimum 5 days, maximum 120 days a spell. Available to female servants and single male parents
flashcards.src: Rule 43C, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: 730 days in the entire service; 120 days

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 44 attach to work related injury or illness leave (WRIIL)?
flashcards.back: 6 + 12 months (civil); 6 + 24 (CAPF officers); no limit for CAPF below officer rank
flashcards.expl: WRIIL replaced the old special disability leave and hospital leave from 14.12.2018. Full pay during hospitalisation; beyond it, 6 months full pay plus 12 months half pay for civil servants, 6 + 24 months full pay for CAPF officers, and no limit for CAPF below officer rank. No EL or HPL is credited d
flashcards.src: Rule 44, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 47 attach to seamen's sick leave?
flashcards.back: 6 weeks; 3 months if disabled on duty
flashcards.expl: Seamen's sick leave: six weeks on full pay, extendable to three months if disabled on duty. Malingering or self-indulgence bars the leave.
flashcards.src: Rule 47, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: 6 weeks; 3 months if disabled on duty

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 48 attach to special leave for an inquiry into sexual harassment?
flashcards.back: 90 days
flashcards.expl: Special leave of up to 90 days pending an inquiry into sexual harassment, on the recommendation of the Internal or Local Committee.
flashcards.src: Rule 48, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 49 attach to departmental leave?
flashcards.back: Up to 18 months in the recess
flashcards.expl: Departmental leave is confined to Survey of India field/recess staff and P&T seasonal staff. It runs only while the services are temporarily not required, pays 25% of EL leave salary plus DA, is not debited to the account, and may run up to 18 months in the recess.
flashcards.src: Rule 49, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: Up to 18 months in the recess

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 50 attach to conditions for grant of study leave?
flashcards.back: Five years' service; bond 3 years (5 for CHS)
flashcards.expl: Study leave needs a definite sphere of duties, five years' regular continuous service including probation, a return date at least three years before superannuation, and a bond of three years' service (five for CHS officers on the 36-month route).
flashcards.src: Rule 50, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: Five years' service; bond 3 years (5 for

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 51 attach to maximum study leave?
flashcards.back: 24 months (36 CHS); 12 months at a time
flashcards.expl: Study leave: 24 months in the entire service, ordinarily 12 months at a time; 36 months for CHS officers. The ceiling is inclusive of similar leave under any other rules.
flashcards.src: Rule 51, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: 24 months (36 CHS); 12 months at a time

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 52 attach to application for study leave?
flashcards.back: Before the leave is to commence
flashcards.expl: Study leave is applied for through the proper channel, with the course and the examinations clearly specified. Late details go to the Head of Mission or the sanctioning authority.
flashcards.src: Rule 52, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: Before the leave is to commence

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 53 attach to sanction of study leave and bond?
flashcards.back: Bond before commencement; certificate to the Audit Officer
flashcards.expl: Sanction of study leave needs the Audit Officer's admissibility report, the parent department's concurrence where the servant is on loan, and a bond: Form 7/8 for permanent staff, Form 9/10 for non-permanent staff, executed before the leave begins, with a certificate of execution to the Audit Office
flashcards.src: Rule 53, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 54 attach to accounting and combination of study leave?
flashcards.back: 28 months (36 for Ph.D.) total absence
flashcards.expl: Study leave is not debited against the leave account. Combined absence is capped at 28 months generally and 36 months for a Ph.D. course, and the cap includes vacations.
flashcards.src: Rule 54, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 55 attach to course falling short of the leave?
flashcards.back: At the conclusion of the course
flashcards.expl: If the course ends early, the servant resumes duty unless previous sanction treats the shortfall as ordinary leave.
flashcards.src: Rule 55, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: At the conclusion of the course

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 56 attach to leave salary during study leave?
flashcards.back: Monthly during study leave
flashcards.expl: Study leave salary is the pay last drawn plus DA and HRA as admissible. Scholarships and stipends are adjusted against it, and it never falls below the HPL salary.
flashcards.src: Rule 56, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 57 attach to conditions for study allowance?
flashcards.back: 24 months in all; 14 days for sickness interruptions
flashcards.expl: Study allowance is for study outside India only. Interruptions for convenience earn nothing; up to 14 days at a time for sickness. Vacation during the course is covered, but end-of-course vacation only up to 14 days. The outer limit is 24 months.
flashcards.src: Rule 57, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: 24 months in all; 14 days for sickness i

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 60 attach to allowances in addition to study allowance?
flashcards.back: HRA 180 days
flashcards.expl: HRA for up to 180 days, then only against a certificate. Except HRA, DA and the study allowance, no other allowance is payable during study leave.
flashcards.src: Rule 60, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 61 attach to travelling allowance during study leave?
flashcards.back: Exceptional circumstances
flashcards.expl: TA is not ordinarily payable during study leave. The President may sanction it in exceptional circumstances; for the IA&AD, the C&AG may.
flashcards.src: Rule 61, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 62 attach to cost of fees for study?
flashcards.back: Exceptional cases
flashcards.expl: Fees are ordinarily the servant's own cost; the President may sanction them in exceptional cases, but never where a scholarship, stipend or part-time remuneration is held.
flashcards.src: Rule 62, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 63 attach to refund on quitting service or failing the course?
flashcards.back: Three years after return; interest from the date of demand
flashcards.expl: Quitting without return, or within three years of return, or failing the course, triggers refund of leave salary, study allowance, fees, TA and other expenses, plus interest. The leave is then re-converted into regular leave, with any balance treated as EOL. The President may waive.
flashcards.src: Rule 63, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: Three years after return; interest from

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 64 attach to interpretation?
flashcards.back: As and when a doubt arises
flashcards.expl: Doubts on interpretation go to the Government, and that decision is final.
flashcards.src: Rule 64, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
flashcards.mnemonic: As and when a doubt arises

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 65 attach to power to relax?
flashcards.back: Exceptional cases
flashcards.expl: The President may relax any provision in exceptional cases — a route for exceptions, not for ordinary administration.
flashcards.src: Rule 65, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: What period or figure does Rule 66 attach to repeal and saving?
flashcards.expl: The rules in the Second Schedule are repealed, but leave already earned is saved and acts done under the old rules are deemed done under these rules.
flashcards.src: Rule 66, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 1 (Short title and commencement)?
flashcards.back: President (rule-making authority); administered by DoPT
flashcards.expl: Rule 1 — Short title is Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules, 1972; the rules came into force on 1 June 1972.
flashcards.src: Rule 1 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 2 (Extent of application)?
flashcards.back: Department of Personnel & Training (rule-making); applicability decided by the terms of the post
flashcards.expl: Rule 2 — Applies to Union civil services and posts. Eleven exclusions, clauses (a) to (k): Railways, casual/daily-rated/part-time, contingency-paid, industrial workmen, work-charged, All India Services, locally recruited overseas
flashcards.src: Rule 2 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 3 (Definitions (13 clauses, a to m))?
flashcards.back: Definitions govern the First Schedule, Rules 15, 19, 27, 29 and 32
flashcards.expl: Rule 3 — Thirteen definitions, clauses (a) to (m). The examinable ones are (a) Administrator, (b) Audit Officer, (c) authority competent to grant leave (First Schedule), (d) completed years of service — which expressly includes l
flashcards.src: Rule 3 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R3 → Definitions govern the First Sched

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 4 (Government servants on temporary transfer or foreign service)?
flashcards.back: Transferring authority grants leave; foreign employer for EL up to 120 days
flashcards.expl: Rule 4 — The rules follow the servant on temporary transfer to Railways, a State Government or foreign service within India. Out of India, or on transfer to the Armed Forces, they apply only so far as the terms provide. A servant
flashcards.src: Rule 4 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 5 (Transfer from services or posts governed by other leave rules)?
flashcards.back: Head of Office / Audit Officer (leave account)
flashcards.expl: Rule 5 — Leave already running under another rule-set is completed under that rule-set. The balance at credit is carried forward only so far as Rule 26 allows, and carried-forward leave is exhausted first.
flashcards.src: Rule 5 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R5 → Head of Office / Audit Officer

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 6 (Transfer to an industrial establishment)?
flashcards.back: Head of Office / Accounts Officer
flashcards.expl: Rule 6 — On transfer to an industrial establishment outside these rules, the leave balance is cashed out suo motu, EL and HPL together, capped at 300 days.
flashcards.src: Rule 6 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R6 → Head of Office / Accounts Officer

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 7 (Right to leave)?
flashcards.back: Authority empowered to grant the leave (First Schedule)
flashcards.expl: Rule 7 — Leave is not a matter of right: it may be refused or revoked. The kind of leave cannot be changed to the servant's disadvantage except on his own written request. Even a refusal should be by written order.
flashcards.src: Rule 7 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R7 → Authority empowered to grant the l

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 8 (Regulation of claim to leave)?
flashcards.back: Authority competent to grant leave
flashcards.expl: Rule 8 — The claim is regulated by the rules in force when leave is applied for and granted, not by the rules in force when the leave was earned. This is the classic 240/300 amendment trap.
flashcards.src: Rule 8 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R8 → Authority competent to grant leave

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 9 (Dismissal, removal and resignation)?
flashcards.back: Head of Office
flashcards.expl: Rule 9 — Leave lapses from the date of dismissal, removal or resignation, and no cash equivalent is payable. Exceptions: Rule 39, reinstatement, and a technical resignation through the proper channel.
flashcards.src: Rule 9 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 10 (Commutation of one kind of leave into another)?
flashcards.back: Authority competent to grant leave
flashcards.expl: Rule 10 — One kind of leave may be commuted into another on a request made within 30 days of rejoining; the concession is discretionary and any excess salary is adjusted.
flashcards.src: Rule 10 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R10 → Authority competent to grant leave

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 11 (Combination of leave)?
flashcards.back: Authority competent to grant leave
flashcards.expl: Rule 11 — Any statutory leave may be combined with any other statutory leave. Casual leave is the single exception: the Explanation says it is not 'leave' and cannot be combined with any leave under these rules.
flashcards.src: Rule 11 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R11 → Authority competent to grant leave

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 12 (Maximum continuous leave)?
flashcards.back: President (extension); authority competent to grant leave (within the limit)
flashcards.expl: Rule 12 — Five years is the outer limit of continuous leave; beyond it the servant is deemed to have resigned. Only the President may extend it, on exceptional circumstances.
flashcards.src: Rule 12 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 13 (Service or employment while on leave)?
flashcards.back: President (outside India); appointing authority (within India)
flashcards.expl: Rule 13 — Previous sanction is required for any service or employment during leave. Outside India the sanction is the President's; within India, the appointing authority's. Cancelled LPR is encashable under Rule 39(2) — Rule 13(3)
flashcards.src: Rule 13 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 14 (Application for leave)?
flashcards.back: Authority competent to grant leave (First Schedule)
flashcards.expl: Rule 14 — Leave is applied for in Form 1, and an extension of leave goes in the same Form 1. Where the servant cannot sign, the application may be signed by the persons listed in the rule.
flashcards.src: Rule 14 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R14 → Authority competent to grant leave

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 15 (Leave account)?
flashcards.back: Audit Officer / Head of Office
flashcards.expl: Rule 15 — One account per servant, in Form 2. Who keeps it depends on how the pay is drawn: Audit Officer for Gazetted officers paid through the PAO, Head of Office for Gazetted officers paid directly, Head of Office for all non-G
flashcards.src: Rule 15 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R15 → Audit Officer / Head of Office

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 16 (Verification of title to leave)?
flashcards.back: Audit Officer / Head of Office
flashcards.expl: Rule 16 — Admissibility is verified first. Where that is not possible, provisional sanction is limited to 60 days and is open to later modification.
flashcards.src: Rule 16 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R16 → Audit Officer / Head of Office

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 17 (Leave not granted in certain circumstances)?
flashcards.back: Punishing authority / authority competent to grant leave
flashcards.expl: Rule 17 — Once the punishing authority has decided on dismissal, removal or compulsory retirement, leave cannot be granted. This is a bar, not a discretion.
flashcards.src: Rule 17 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 19 (Leave on medical certificate)?
flashcards.back: Authorised Medical Attendant / Civil Surgeon / Medical Board (per the form)
flashcards.expl: Rule 19 — Medical-certificate leave runs on Form 3 (Gazetted), Form 4 (non-Gazetted), Form 3-A (disability) and Form 5 (fitness to return). The certificate may be waived up to 3 days at a time — and that leave is then not treated
flashcards.src: Rule 19 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 20 (Government servant unlikely to be fit to return to duty)?
flashcards.back: Authority competent to grant leave on the medical authority's certificate
flashcards.expl: Rule 20 — Where recovery is uncertain, leave up to 12 months at a time, extended on fresh certificates. Where the servant is permanently incapacitated and already on leave, the cap is 6 months.
flashcards.src: Rule 20 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R20 → Authority competent to grant leave

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 21 (Commencement and termination of leave)?
flashcards.back: Head of Office
flashcards.expl: Rule 21 — Leave begins on the day the charge is handed over and ends the day before the charge is resumed. A holiday in between does not shift either end-date.
flashcards.src: Rule 21 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 22 (Holidays with leave)?
flashcards.back: Authority competent to grant leave
flashcards.expl: Rule 22 — Holidays may be prefixed or suffixed and are not debited. On medical-certificate leave the concession is automatic. The Note brings comp-off within 'holiday' for prefixing and suffixing.
flashcards.src: Rule 22 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R22 → Authority competent to grant leave

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 23 (Recall to duty)?
flashcards.back: Authority competent to grant leave
flashcards.expl: Rule 23 — Sub-rules (1) and (2) are deleted; sub-rule (3) survives. Recall is compulsory in every case, and the servant draws TA and leave salary until he joins.
flashcards.src: Rule 23 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R23 → Authority competent to grant leave

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 24 (Return from leave)?
flashcards.back: Authority competent to grant leave / appointing authority (LPR)
flashcards.expl: Rule 24 — Permission is needed to return. LPR needs the appointing authority's consent. Medical-certificate leave requires a Form 5 fitness certificate on return.
flashcards.src: Rule 24 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R24 → Authority competent to grant leave

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 25 (Absence after expiry of leave)?
flashcards.back: Head of Office
flashcards.expl: Rule 25 — Overstay is debited as HPL to the extent of the balance, then as EOL. No leave salary at all for the overstay, and wilful absence invites CCA action.
flashcards.src: Rule 25 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 26 (Earned leave)?
flashcards.back: Ministry/Department, Administrator, CAG, Head of Department, appointing authority or delegated subordinate (First Schedule)
flashcards.expl: Rule 26 — Earned leave: 15 days credited in advance on 1 January and 1 July (30 days a year); accumulation ceiling 300 days; 285-day buffer under which the next credit is held apart; 180 days at a time in India, 150 for the Except
flashcards.src: Rule 26 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 27 (Calculation of earned leave)?
flashcards.back: Audit Officer / Head of Office (leave account)
flashcards.expl: Rule 27 — The pro-rata engine. Credit is 2 1/2 days per completed month, applied in the joining half-year and the exit cases: retirement or resignation up to the date; removal or dismissal only up to the end of the preceding month
flashcards.src: Rule 27 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R27 → Audit Officer / Head of Office

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 28 (Earned leave in vacation departments)?
flashcards.back: Head of Department (vacation schedule); leave-granting authority
flashcards.expl: Rule 28 — Vacation departments start from a 5 + 5 = 10 day base, and add a proportionate share of 20 days for vacation not taken, up to 30 days a year. No vacation at all in a year means Rule 26 applies. The 300-day ceiling is unc
flashcards.src: Rule 28 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 29 (Half pay leave)?
flashcards.back: Ministry/Department, Administrator, CAG, Head of Department, appointing authority or delegated subordinate
flashcards.expl: Rule 29 — Half pay leave: 10 days credited per half-year (20 a year), earned at 5/3 days per completed month, with no accumulation ceiling. Dies non costs 1/18th of the period, capped at 10 days. It may be taken on medical grounds
flashcards.src: Rule 29 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 30 (Commuted leave)?
flashcards.back: Authority competent to grant leave (First Schedule)
flashcards.expl: Rule 30 — One day of commuted leave buys full pay at the price of two days of half pay leave. It needs a medical certificate, and satisfaction that the servant will return. Study commutation up to 180 days is the certificate-free
flashcards.src: Rule 30 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R30 → Authority competent to grant leave

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 31 (Leave not due)?
flashcards.back: Authority competent to grant leave
flashcards.expl: Rule 31 — Leave not due is HPL advanced against future earnings, capped at 360 days in the entire service, on medical certificate, for permanent and quasi-permanent staff. Temporary staff get the same 360 days only for TB, leprosy
flashcards.src: Rule 31 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R31 → Authority competent to grant leave

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 32 (Extraordinary leave)?
flashcards.back: Authority competent to grant leave; President for cases beyond sub-rule (2)
flashcards.expl: Rule 32 — EOL carries no leave salary. The sub-rule (2) ladder is 3 months general, 6 months with one year's service plus a medical certificate, 18 months for the specified diseases, and 24 months for study in the public interest
flashcards.src: Rule 32 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R32 → Authority competent to grant leave

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 33 (Leave to probationers and apprentices)?
flashcards.back: Appointing authority / authority competent to grant leave
flashcards.expl: Rule 33 — A probationer cannot be carried on leave beyond the probation period, except on EOL. An apprentice gets one month of medical-certificate leave on half pay a year, plus EOL.
flashcards.src: Rule 33 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 34 (Re-employment and counting of past service)?
flashcards.back: Head of Office / Audit Officer
flashcards.expl: Rule 34 — Past service counts for leave wherever it counts for pension; the leave account follows the pension counting rather than a separate test.
flashcards.src: Rule 34 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R34 → Head of Office / Audit Officer

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 38 (Leave preparatory to retirement)?
flashcards.back: Appointing authority; lending authority concurrence in foreign service
flashcards.expl: Rule 38 — LPR is the whole balance taken at the end: EL up to 300 days plus HPL, up to the date of retirement. EOL is expressly outside LPR. Where LPR is cancelled under Rule 13(3)(b), it is encashable under Rule 39(2).
flashcards.src: Rule 38 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 38A (Earned leave encashment with LTC)?
flashcards.back: Head of Office / Pay & Accounts Officer
flashcards.expl: Rule 38A — LTC encashment: 10 days per occasion, 60 days in the career, and at least 30 days of EL must remain after encashment. If the LTC is not availed, the money comes back with interest at 2% above the PF rate.
flashcards.src: Rule 38A read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R38A → Head of Office / Pay & Accounts Of

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 39 (Cash in lieu of leave on retirement)?
flashcards.back: Head of Office / Pay & Accounts Officer
flashcards.expl: Rule 39 — On retirement the authority acts suo motu: EL and HPL are both encashed, together capped at 300 days, on the retirement-date pay plus DA. HPL cannot be commuted to top up an EL shortfall. Nothing is paid on resignation,
flashcards.src: Rule 39 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R39 → Head of Office / Pay & Accounts Of

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 39A (Cash equivalent on death in service)?
flashcards.back: Head of Office (payment to the family)
flashcards.expl: Rule 39A — Death in service: the family gets cash equivalent of up to 300 days, computed as if the servant had gone on earned leave on the day after death. LTC encashment already taken is subtracted from the 300-day ceiling, and th
flashcards.src: Rule 39A read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 39B (Cash equivalent on invalidation)?
flashcards.back: Head of Office
flashcards.expl: Rule 39B — Invalidation on permanent incapacity: EL and HPL both encashed, 300-day cap, suo motu. A non-permanent or non-quasi-permanent servant gets EL only — no HPL.
flashcards.src: Rule 39B read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 39C (Order of payment of cash equivalent)?
flashcards.back: Head of Office
flashcards.expl: Rule 39C — The succession ladder for money not yet received: widow or husband, son, unmarried daughter, widowed daughter, father, mother, married daughter, minor brother, unmarried sister, widowed sister, then the eldest child of t
flashcards.src: Rule 39C read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 39D (Cash equivalent on permanent absorption in a PSU)?
flashcards.back: Head of Office
flashcards.expl: Rule 39D — PSU absorption: earned leave only, up to 300 days, suo motu. HPL is not encashed. The body must be wholly or substantially owned or controlled by the Central or a State Government.
flashcards.src: Rule 39D read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 40 (Leave salary)?
flashcards.back: Head of Office / Pay & Accounts Officer
flashcards.expl: Rule 40 — The master rate card: EL full pay, HPL and LND half pay, commuted leave full pay, EOL nothing. DA follows; HRA applies on the stated conditions.
flashcards.src: Rule 40 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R40 → Head of Office / Pay & Accounts Of

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 41 (Drawal of leave salary)?
flashcards.back: Head of Office / Pay & Accounts Officer
flashcards.expl: Rule 41 — Leave salary is drawn in rupees, in India — even where the servant is on leave abroad.
flashcards.src: Rule 41 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R41 → Head of Office / Pay & Accounts Of

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 42 (Advance of leave salary)?
flashcards.back: Head of Office
flashcards.expl: Rule 42 — Advance of leave salary: leave of at least 30 days, advance up to one month's pay and allowances computed on the leave salary admissible, less statutory deductions.
flashcards.src: Rule 42 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 43 (Maternity leave)?
flashcards.back: Ministry/Department, Administrator, CAG, Head of Department, appointing authority or delegated subordinate
flashcards.expl: Rule 43 — Maternity leave: 180 days on full pay for a female servant with fewer than two surviving children; 45 days for miscarriage or abortion, irrespective of the number of children. It is not debited to the leave account, may
flashcards.src: Rule 43 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 43A (Paternity leave)?
flashcards.back: Ministry/Department, Administrator, CAG, Head of Department, appointing authority or delegated subordinate
flashcards.expl: Rule 43A — Paternity leave: 15 days for a male servant with fewer than two surviving children, availed within the window from 15 days before delivery to six months after it. The leave lapses if not taken in that window.
flashcards.src: Rule 43A read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 43AA (Paternity leave on adoption)?
flashcards.back: Ministry/Department, Administrator, CAG, Head of Department, appointing authority
flashcards.expl: Rule 43AA — Paternity leave on adoption: 15 days, on a valid adoption of a child below one year, availed within six months of the adoption.
flashcards.src: Rule 43AA read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 43B (Child adoption leave)?
flashcards.back: Ministry/Department, Administrator, CAG, Head of Department, appointing authority
flashcards.expl: Rule 43B — Child adoption leave: 180 days for a female servant with fewer than two surviving children, on a valid adoption of a child below one year. Not debited to the account.
flashcards.src: Rule 43B read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 43C (Child care leave)?
flashcards.back: Ministry/Department, Administrator, CAG, Head of Department, appointing authority
flashcards.expl: Rule 43C — Child care leave: 730 days in the entire service for the two eldest surviving children, at 100% pay for the first 365 days and 80% for the next 365. Spells: 3 a year normally, 6 for a single female parent, minimum 5 days
flashcards.src: Rule 43C read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 44 (Work related injury or illness leave (WRIIL))?
flashcards.back: Ministry/Department, Administrator, CAG, Head of Department, appointing authority
flashcards.expl: Rule 44 — WRIIL replaced the old special disability leave and hospital leave from 14.12.2018. Full pay during hospitalisation; beyond it, 6 months full pay plus 12 months half pay for civil servants, 6 + 24 months full pay for CAP
flashcards.src: Rule 44 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 47 (Seamen's sick leave)?
flashcards.back: Head of Department
flashcards.expl: Rule 47 — Seamen's sick leave: six weeks on full pay, extendable to three months if disabled on duty. Malingering or self-indulgence bars the leave.
flashcards.src: Rule 47 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 48 (Special leave for an inquiry into sexual harassment)?
flashcards.back: Ministry/Department (on the Committee's recommendation)
flashcards.expl: Rule 48 — Special leave of up to 90 days pending an inquiry into sexual harassment, on the recommendation of the Internal or Local Committee.
flashcards.src: Rule 48 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 49 (Departmental leave)?
flashcards.back: Head of Party / Head of Office
flashcards.expl: Rule 49 — Departmental leave is confined to Survey of India field/recess staff and P&T seasonal staff. It runs only while the services are temporarily not required, pays 25% of EL leave salary plus DA, is not debited to the accoun
flashcards.src: Rule 49 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R49 → Head of Party / Head of Office

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 50 (Conditions for grant of study leave)?
flashcards.back: Ministry/Department, Administrator or CAG (First Schedule — study leave)
flashcards.expl: Rule 50 — Study leave needs a definite sphere of duties, five years' regular continuous service including probation, a return date at least three years before superannuation, and a bond of three years' service (five for CHS office
flashcards.src: Rule 50 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 51 (Maximum study leave)?
flashcards.back: Ministry/Department, Administrator or CAG
flashcards.expl: Rule 51 — Study leave: 24 months in the entire service, ordinarily 12 months at a time; 36 months for CHS officers. The ceiling is inclusive of similar leave under any other rules.
flashcards.src: Rule 51 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 52 (Application for study leave)?
flashcards.back: Head of Department / Ministry / Administrator / CAG
flashcards.expl: Rule 52 — Study leave is applied for through the proper channel, with the course and the examinations clearly specified. Late details go to the Head of Mission or the sanctioning authority.
flashcards.src: Rule 52 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R52 → Head of Department / Ministry / Ad

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 53 (Sanction of study leave and bond)?
flashcards.back: Ministry/Department, Administrator or CAG
flashcards.expl: Rule 53 — Sanction of study leave needs the Audit Officer's admissibility report, the parent department's concurrence where the servant is on loan, and a bond: Form 7/8 for permanent staff, Form 9/10 for non-permanent staff, execu
flashcards.src: Rule 53 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 54 (Accounting and combination of study leave)?
flashcards.back: Audit Officer / sanctioning authority
flashcards.expl: Rule 54 — Study leave is not debited against the leave account. Combined absence is capped at 28 months generally and 36 months for a Ph.D. course, and the cap includes vacations.
flashcards.src: Rule 54 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 55 (Course falling short of the leave)?
flashcards.back: Ministry/Department, Administrator or CAG
flashcards.expl: Rule 55 — If the course ends early, the servant resumes duty unless previous sanction treats the shortfall as ordinary leave.
flashcards.src: Rule 55 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 56 (Leave salary during study leave)?
flashcards.back: Head of Office / Pay & Accounts Officer
flashcards.expl: Rule 56 — Study leave salary is the pay last drawn plus DA and HRA as admissible. Scholarships and stipends are adjusted against it, and it never falls below the HPL salary.
flashcards.src: Rule 56 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R56 → Head of Office / Pay & Accounts Of

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 57 (Conditions for study allowance)?
flashcards.back: Ministry/Department / Administrator / CAG
flashcards.expl: Rule 57 — Study allowance is for study outside India only. Interruptions for convenience earn nothing; up to 14 days at a time for sickness. Vacation during the course is covered, but end-of-course vacation only up to 14 days. The
flashcards.src: Rule 57 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 60 (Allowances in addition to study allowance)?
flashcards.back: Head of Office
flashcards.expl: Rule 60 — HRA for up to 180 days, then only against a certificate. Except HRA, DA and the study allowance, no other allowance is payable during study leave.
flashcards.src: Rule 60 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 61 (Travelling allowance during study leave)?
flashcards.back: President; C&AG for the IA&AD
flashcards.expl: Rule 61 — TA is not ordinarily payable during study leave. The President may sanction it in exceptional circumstances; for the IA&AD, the C&AG may.
flashcards.src: Rule 61 read with the First Schedule
flashcards.mnemonic: R61 → President; C&AG for the IA&AD

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 62 (Cost of fees for study)?
flashcards.back: President
flashcards.expl: Rule 62 — Fees are ordinarily the servant's own cost; the President may sanction them in exceptional cases, but never where a scholarship, stipend or part-time remuneration is held.
flashcards.src: Rule 62 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 63 (Refund on quitting service or failing the course)?
flashcards.back: President (waiver); sanctioning authority (recovery)
flashcards.expl: Rule 63 — Quitting without return, or within three years of return, or failing the course, triggers refund of leave salary, study allowance, fees, TA and other expenses, plus interest. The leave is then re-converted into regular l
flashcards.src: Rule 63 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 64 (Interpretation)?
flashcards.back: Government (DoPT)
flashcards.expl: Rule 64 — Doubts on interpretation go to the Government, and that decision is final.
flashcards.src: Rule 64 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 65 (Power to relax)?
flashcards.back: President
flashcards.expl: Rule 65 — The President may relax any provision in exceptional cases — a route for exceptions, not for ordinary administration.
flashcards.src: Rule 65 read with the First Schedule

flashcards.front: Who acts under Rule 66 (Repeal and saving)?
flashcards.back: President / Government
flashcards.expl: Rule 66 — The rules in the Second Schedule are repealed, but leave already earned is saved and acts done under the old rules are deemed done under these rules.
flashcards.src: Rule 66 read with the First Schedule

modules.title: Rules 1–3: Preliminary
modules.summary: Short title is Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules, 1972; the rules came into force on 1 June 1972. Applies to Union civil services and posts. Eleven exclusions, clauses (a) to (k): Railways, casual/daily-rated/part-time, contingency-paid, industrial workmen, work-charged, All India Services, locally recruited overseas staff, contract staff (unless the contract provides otherwise), persons covered by special constitutional or statutory provisions, FR/CSR-governed staff, and limited-duration State deputationists. Thirteen definitions, clauses (a) to (m). The examinable ones are (a) Administrator, (b) Audit Officer, (c) authority competent to grant leave (First Schedule), (d) completed years of service — which expressly includes leave, including EOL, and (e) date of retirement — the afternoon of the last day of the month of attaining retirement age.
key_facts: Rule 1: In force from 01.06.1972
Rule 1: Title: Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules, 1972.
Rule 1: Commencement: 1 June 1972 — not the date of the title year, and not 1 April.
Rule 2: Continuous
Rule 2: Applies to Government servants appointed to civil services and posts in connection with the affairs of the Union.
Rule 2: Exclusions run (a) to (k) — 11 clauses in all.
Rule 3: Date of retirement: afternoon of the last day of the month
Rule 3: Administrator = Administrator of a Union Territory, whatever the designation (Lt Governor or Administrator).
Rule 3: Audit Officer is identified by circle, not by designation.
modules.traps: Rule 1: Answering 'in force from 1972' generically, or dating commencement to 1 April 1972. Rule 2: 'Railway servants are covered by the Leave Rules' or 'IAS officers follow this rule-book' — both wrong; clauses (a) and (f) exclude them. Contract staff are not always excluded: clause (h) yields where the contract provides otherwise. Rule 3: 'Retirement takes effect on the birthday' — wrong, it is the afternoon of the month's last day. 'EOL does not count for continuous service' — wrong, clause (d) expressly includes it.

modules.title: Rules 4–7: transfers, foreign service and the right to leave
modules.summary: The rules follow the servant on temporary transfer to Railways, a State Government or foreign service within India. Out of India, or on transfer to the Armed Forces, they apply only so far as the terms provide. A servant on foreign service with a foreign employer may be granted earned leave of not more than 120 days at a time. Leave already running under another rule-set is completed under that rule-set. The balance at credit is carried forward only so far as Rule 26 allows, and carried-forward leave is exhausted first. On transfer to an industrial establishment outside these rules, the leave balance is cashed out suo motu, EL and HPL together, capped at 300 days. Leave is not a matter of right: it may be refused or revoked. The kind of leave cannot be changed to the servant's disadvantage except on his own written request. Even a refusal should be by written order.
key_facts: Rule 4: EL 120 days at a time with a foreign employer
Rule 4: Rules continue to apply on temporary transfer to Railways or a State Government.
Rule 4: Rules continue to apply on foreign service within India.
Rule 5: Carried forward within the Rule 26 ceiling
Rule 5: Leave in progress is regulated by the old rule-set until it expires.
Rule 5: Credit carried forward is limited by the Rule 26 ceiling.
Rule 6: Suo motu on the date of transfer
Rule 6: Cash equivalent covers earned leave and half pay leave at credit.
Rule 6: Ceiling: 300 days.
Rule 7: No time limit — discretionary
modules.traps: Rule 4: 'Foreign service ends the application of the Leave Rules' — wrong within India. 'Foreign employer can sanction any leave' — wrong, EL is capped at 120 days at a time. Rule 5: Assuming the entire old balance survives transfer regardless of the 300-day ceiling. Rule 6: 'Servant must apply for the cash equivalent' — wrong, it is suo motu. 'Ceiling is 240 days' — wrong, 300. Rule 7: 'Once sanctioned, leave can never be revoked' — wrong. 'The authority may convert EL into EOL on its own' — wrong without the servant's written request.

modules.title: Rules 8–13: the arithmetic of old balances
modules.summary: The claim is regulated by the rules in force when leave is applied for and granted, not by the rules in force when the leave was earned. This is the classic 240/300 amendment trap. Leave lapses from the date of dismissal, removal or resignation, and no cash equivalent is payable. Exceptions: Rule 39, reinstatement, and a technical resignation through the proper channel. One kind of leave may be commuted into another on a request made within 30 days of rejoining; the concession is discretionary and any excess salary is adjusted. Any statutory leave may be combined with any other statutory leave. Casual leave is the single exception: the Explanation says it is not 'leave' and cannot be combined with any leave under these rules. Five years is the outer limit of continuous leave; beyond it the servant is deemed to have resigned. Only the President may extend it, on exceptional circumstances.
key_facts: Rule 8: Rules as in force on the date of application and grant
Rule 8: The governing date is the date of application and grant.
Rule 9: Lapse takes effect from the date of dismissal, removal or resignation
Rule 9: Leave lapses on dismissal, removal or resignation.
Rule 9: No cash equivalent is admissible on those events.
Rule 10: 30 days from rejoining duty
Rule 10: Request must be made within 30 days of rejoining duty.
Rule 10: The authority has discretion — commutation is not a right.
Rule 11: Rule 11 allows combination of any statutory leave with any other.
Rule 11: The Explanation excludes casual leave from the definition of leave.
modules.traps: Rule 8: Computing an old balance under the ceiling in force when it was earned — the 240/300 trap. Rule 9: 'Resignation with a technical label still forfeits leave' — wrong if it is through the proper channel. 'Cash equivalent is paid on resignation' — wrong. Rule 10: Confusing Rule 10 commutation (leave type conversion) with Rule 30 commuted leave (HPL taken at full pay with double debit). Rule 11: 'CL can be combined with EL' — wrong, the Explanation bars it. 'Study leave cannot be combined with EOL' — the bar is on the 28/36-month absence, not the combination.

modules.title: Rules 14–17: application, account and verification
modules.summary: Leave is applied for in Form 1, and an extension of leave goes in the same Form 1. Where the servant cannot sign, the application may be signed by the persons listed in the rule. One account per servant, in Form 2. Who keeps it depends on how the pay is drawn: Audit Officer for Gazetted officers paid through the PAO, Head of Office for Gazetted officers paid directly, Head of Office for all non-Gazetted staff. Admissibility is verified first. Where that is not possible, provisional sanction is limited to 60 days and is open to later modification. Once the punishing authority has decided on dismissal, removal or compulsory retirement, leave cannot be granted. This is a bar, not a discretion.
key_facts: Rule 14: Apply before the leave is to commence; extension before expiry
Rule 14: Form 1 is the prescribed form for leave and for extension of leave.
Rule 15: Continuous maintenance
Rule 15: Form 2 is the form of the leave account.
Rule 15: Gazetted (pay drawn by Audit Officer): Audit Officer keeps the account.
Rule 16: Provisional sanction 60 days (GSR No. 1422, 21.11.1979)
Rule 16: Admissibility report precedes the sanction.
Rule 16: Provisional sanction: maximum 60 days.
Rule 17: From the date of the competent authority's decision
Rule 17: The bar applies once the decision to dismiss, remove or compulsorily retire is taken.
modules.traps: Rule 14: 'Extension of leave needs a fresh form other than Form 1' — wrong. 'Medical certificate is the leave application' — no, Form 1 is. Rule 15: 'CAG keeps every leave account' — wrong, the Audit Officer (accounts side) does, and only for the gazetted-through-PAO route. Rule 16: 'Provisional sanction is final' — wrong, it is verified and may be modified. '90 days' — wrong, 60. Rule 17: 'Leave may still be granted at the authority's discretion after a decision to remove' — wrong, it is barred.

modules.title: Rules 19–25: medical certificates and the return to duty
modules.summary: Medical-certificate leave runs on Form 3 (Gazetted), Form 4 (non-Gazetted), Form 3-A (disability) and Form 5 (fitness to return). The certificate may be waived up to 3 days at a time — and that leave is then not treated as leave on medical certificate. Where recovery is uncertain, leave up to 12 months at a time, extended on fresh certificates. Where the servant is permanently incapacitated and already on leave, the cap is 6 months. Leave begins on the day the charge is handed over and ends the day before the charge is resumed. A holiday in between does not shift either end-date. Holidays may be prefixed or suffixed and are not debited. On medical-certificate leave the concession is automatic. The Note brings comp-off within 'holiday' for prefixing and suffixing. Sub-rules (1) and (2) are deleted; sub-rule (3) survives. Recall is compulsory in every case, and the servant draws TA and lea
key_facts: Rule 19: Waiver up to 3 days at a time
Rule 19: Form 3: Gazetted. Form 4: non-Gazetted. Form 3-A: disability. Form 5: fitness to return.
Rule 19: Waiver up to 3 days at a time.
Rule 20: 12 months at a time; 6 months where permanently incapacitated
Rule 20: Leave at a time: 12 months where recovery is uncertain.
Rule 20: Permanent incapacity while already on leave: 6 months.
Rule 21: Charge handover / resumption dates
Rule 21: Commencement: date of handing over charge.
Rule 21: Termination: day before resuming charge.
Rule 22: Holidays do not count against leave.
modules.traps: Rule 19: Swapping Form 3 and Form 4 between Gazetted and non-Gazetted staff; treating the 3-day waiver as still 'medical certificate leave'. Rule 20: Swapping the 12-month and 6-month limits. Rule 21: 'Leave ends on the day charge is resumed' — wrong, it ends the day before. Rule 22: 'Holidays are debited to the leave account' — wrong. 'On medical-certificate leave the servant must ask for prefixing' — wrong, it is automatic.

modules.title: Rule 26: earned leave, the ceiling and the 285-day buffer
modules.summary: Earned leave: 15 days credited in advance on 1 January and 1 July (30 days a year); accumulation ceiling 300 days; 285-day buffer under which the next credit is held apart; 180 days at a time in India, 150 for the Exception category, 300 if spent abroad in the specified countries.
key_facts: Rule 26: Credited 1 January and 1 July; 180 days at a time in India
Rule 26: EL credit: 15 days in advance on 1 January and 1 July.
Rule 26: Annual credit: 30 days.
modules.traps: Rule 26: 'EL is credited monthly' — wrong, half-yearly. 'Ceiling 240 days' — wrong, 300. 'Buffer is 225' — wrong, 285. 'At a time always 300' — wrong, 180 in India. 'Joining time has no ceiling impact' — wrong, EL + joining time stays within 300.

modules.title: Rule 27: the pro-rata engine
modules.summary: The pro-rata engine. Credit is 2 1/2 days per completed month, applied in the joining half-year and the exit cases: retirement or resignation up to the date; removal or dismissal only up to the end of the preceding month; death up to the date of death. EOL and dies non cost 1/10th of the period, capped at 15 days. Fractions round to the nearest day.
key_facts: Rule 27: Applied at the next half-year credit; exit credit up to the relevant date
Rule 27: Rate: 2 1/2 days per completed calendar month.
Rule 27: Retirement or resignation: up to the date.
modules.traps: Rule 27: '5 days a month' — wrong, 2 1/2. 'EOL penalty 1/5th' — wrong, 1/10th, max 15. 'Removal month counts' — wrong. 'No credit on death' — wrong, up to the date of death. 'Always round up' — wrong, nearest day.

modules.title: Rule 28: vacation departments
modules.summary: Vacation departments start from a 5 + 5 = 10 day base, and add a proportionate share of 20 days for vacation not taken, up to 30 days a year. No vacation at all in a year means Rule 26 applies. The 300-day ceiling is unchanged.
key_facts: Rule 28: Half-yearly 5 days; year = 12 months of actual duty
Rule 28: Base credit: 5 days per half-year (10 a year).
Rule 28: Additional EL: 20 × (vacation days not taken ÷ full vacation days).
modules.traps: Rule 28: 'Vacation department gets the same 30 days base' — wrong, 5 + 5. 'Year means calendar year' — wrong. 'Vacation + EL has no limit' — wrong, Rule 26 admissible EL governs.

modules.title: Rule 29: half pay leave and the 1/18th penalty
modules.summary: Half pay leave: 10 days credited per half-year (20 a year), earned at 5/3 days per completed month, with no accumulation ceiling. Dies non costs 1/18th of the period, capped at 10 days. It may be taken on medical grounds or private affairs.
key_facts: Rule 29: Credited 1 January and 1 July
Rule 29: HPL credit: 10 days per half-year, 1 January and 1 July.
Rule 29: Annual credit: 20 days.
modules.traps: Rule 29: 'HPL credited at 2 1/2 days a month' — wrong, that is EL. 'HPL capped at 300 days' — wrong, no ceiling. 'HPL only on medical grounds' — wrong, private affairs too. 'Dies non penalty 1/10th' — wrong, 1/18th, max 10.

modules.title: Rule 30: commuted leave, full pay at a double price
modules.summary: One day of commuted leave buys full pay at the price of two days of half pay leave. It needs a medical certificate, and satisfaction that the servant will return. Study commutation up to 180 days is the certificate-free route. Non-return triggers recovery of the difference unless the retirement is on ill-health or death.
key_facts: Rule 30: Study commutation 180 days in the entire service
Rule 30: Debit: twice the commuted leave against HPL due.
Rule 30: Maximum commuted leave: half of HPL due.
modules.traps: Rule 30: 'Commuted leave is paid at half pay' — wrong, full pay with double debit. 'Debit equals the leave taken' — wrong, twice. 'No medical certificate ever' — wrong. 'No recovery on resignation' — wrong, recovery applies.

modules.title: Rule 31: leave not due
modules.summary: Leave not due is HPL advanced against future earnings, capped at 360 days in the entire service, on medical certificate, for permanent and quasi-permanent staff. Temporary staff get the same 360 days only for TB, leprosy, cancer or mental illness. It is not available for leave preparatory to retirement.
key_facts: Rule 31: Half pay leave likely to be earned later; 360 days in all under sub-rule (1-A)
Rule 31: Maximum: 360 days in the entire service.
Rule 31: Eligible: permanent or quasi-permanent, other than military officers.
modules.traps: Rule 31: 'LND maximum 180 days' — wrong, 360. 'Temporary staff get LND for any illness' — wrong. 'LND on private affairs' — wrong, medical only. 'LND for LPR' — wrong. 'LND at full pay' — wrong, half pay.

modules.title: Rule 32: extraordinary leave, the 3/6/18/24 ladder
modules.summary: EOL carries no leave salary. The sub-rule (2) ladder is 3 months general, 6 months with one year's service plus a medical certificate, 18 months for the specified diseases, and 24 months for study in the public interest with three years' service. Study EOL beyond the limits needs a Form 6 bond.
key_facts: Rule 32: 3 / 6 / 18 / 24 months, according to service and circumstances
Rule 32: EOL may be taken when no other leave is due, or when the servant applies in writing.
Rule 32: 3 months: general limit for non-permanent staff.
modules.traps: Rule 32: 'EOL carries leave salary' — wrong, none. 'Maximum EOL 12 months' — wrong, 24 for study and 18 for the specified diseases. 'Study EOL needs one year's service' — wrong, three. 'EOL only when no other leave is due' — wrong, a written request also works.

modules.title: Rules 33–34: probationers, apprentices and re-employment
modules.summary: A probationer cannot be carried on leave beyond the probation period, except on EOL. An apprentice gets one month of medical-certificate leave on half pay a year, plus EOL. Past service counts for leave wherever it counts for pension; the leave account follows the pension counting rather than a separate test.
key_facts: Rule 33: Probation period; apprentice one month a year
Rule 33: Probationer's leave cannot run beyond the probation period, except EOL.
Rule 33: Apprentice: one month on half pay on medical certificate per year.
Rule 34: At the time of re-employment
Rule 34: Past service counts for leave where it counts for pension.
modules.traps: Rule 33: 'A probationer may take EL beyond probation' — wrong. 'Apprentice gets full pay' — wrong, half pay. Rule 34: 'Re-employment automatically carries forward the whole leave balance' — only where the service counts for pension.

modules.title: Rule 38: leave preparatory to retirement
modules.summary: LPR is the whole balance taken at the end: EL up to 300 days plus HPL, up to the date of retirement. EOL is expressly outside LPR. Where LPR is cancelled under Rule 13(3)(b), it is encashable under Rule 39(2).
key_facts: Rule 38: Up to the date of retirement
Rule 38: EL due up to 300 days plus HPL due, up to the date of retirement.
Rule 38: Cancelled LPR is encashable under Rule 39(2).
modules.traps: Rule 38: 'LPR can include EOL' — wrong. 'LPR EL limit is 240 days' — wrong, amended to 300 in 2004. 'LND can extend LPR' — wrong.

modules.title: Rule 38-A: LTC encashment
modules.summary: LTC encashment: 10 days per occasion, 60 days in the career, and at least 30 days of EL must remain after encashment. If the LTC is not availed, the money comes back with interest at 2% above the PF rate.
key_facts: Rule 38A: Per LTC occasion; 60 days per career
Rule 38A: 10 days per LTC occasion.
Rule 38A: 60 days in the entire career.
modules.traps: Rule 38A: '60 per occasion' — wrong, 10. 'Career total 300' — wrong, 60. 'No minimum balance' — wrong, 30 days must remain.

modules.title: Rule 39: cash in lieu of leave
modules.summary: On retirement the authority acts suo motu: EL and HPL are both encashed, together capped at 300 days, on the retirement-date pay plus DA. HPL cannot be commuted to top up an EL shortfall. Nothing is paid on resignation, dismissal or removal — that is Rule 9.
key_facts: Rule 39: Suo motu on the date of retirement
Rule 39: EL and HPL are both encashed, capped at 300 days combined.
Rule 39: Cash equivalent = (Pay + DA) × days ÷ 30.
modules.traps: Rule 39: 'HPL can be commuted to top up EL' — wrong. 'Cash equivalent is at the last basic pay only' — wrong, pay plus DA. 'Resignation earns encashment' — wrong, Rule 9 lapses the balance.

modules.title: Rules 39-A to 39-D: death, invalidation and PSU absorption
modules.summary: Death in service: the family gets cash equivalent of up to 300 days, computed as if the servant had gone on earned leave on the day after death. LTC encashment already taken is subtracted from the 300-day ceiling, and there is no DCRG set-off. Invalidation on permanent incapacity: EL and HPL both encashed, 300-day cap, suo motu. A non-permanent or non-quasi-permanent servant gets EL only — no HPL.
