cases.title: Case 1: Earned leave at a time
cases.facts: In the Department of Administrative Reforms, a Private Secretary holding 296 days of earned leave applies for 210 days of earned leave to be spent at his home town in Kerala. The establishment section is unsure whether the sanction can issue at the requested length.
cases.issue: What is the correct position under Rule 26(2)(i) and 26(3), CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972?
cases.action: 180 days — no servant employed in India may be granted more at a time.
cases.authority: Head of Office / competent authority as fixed by the First Schedule
cases.conclusion: From a 296-day balance, grant 180 days — then a fresh grant may be considered.
cases.exam_q: In the Department of Administrative Reforms, a Private Secretary holding 296 days of earned leave applies for 210 days of earned leave to be spent at his home town in Kerala. The establishment section is unsure whether the sanction can issue at the requested length. (Answer: 180 days — no servant employed in India may be granted more at a time.)

cases.title: Case 2: 285-day buffer
cases.facts: In the Ministry of Finance, a Section Officer held 292 days of earned leave on 31 December 2025 and took 8 days of earned leave in February 2026. The leave section has to fix his balance on 30 June 2026 for a pension paper.
cases.issue: What is the correct position under Rule 26(1)(b), proviso, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972?
cases.action: 299 days — 292 held, plus the 15-day credit less the 8 days set off.
cases.authority: Head of Office / competent authority as fixed by the First Schedule
cases.conclusion: 292 held + (15 − 8) posted = 299 days.
cases.exam_q: In the Ministry of Finance, a Section Officer held 292 days of earned leave on 31 December 2025 and took 8 days of earned leave in February 2026. The leave section has to fix his balance on 30 June 2026 for a pension paper. (Answer: 299 days — 292 held, plus the 15-day credit less the 8 days set off.)

cases.title: Case 3: Leave not due
cases.facts: In the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, a quasi-permanent Assistant holding 40 days of half pay leave applies for 120 days of leave not due for a spinal surgery, with a medical certificate and a favourable prognosis from the treating hospital.
cases.issue: What is the correct position under Rule 31(1), CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972?
cases.action: Limited to the half pay he will earn later, within the 360-day ceiling.
cases.authority: Head of Office / competent authority as fixed by the First Schedule
cases.conclusion: LND = HPL advanced against future earnings; 360 days lifetime.
cases.exam_q: In the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, a quasi-permanent Assistant holding 40 days of half pay leave applies for 120 days of leave not due for a spinal surgery, with a medical certificate and a favourable prognosis from the treating hospital. (Answer: Limited to the half pay he will earn later, within the 360-day ceiling.)

cases.title: Case 4: Commuted leave recovery
cases.facts: In the Ministry of External Affairs, an officer took 40 days of commuted leave for an illness, and on return tendered his resignation without rejoining duty, the resignation being accepted on personal grounds.
cases.issue: What is the correct position under Rule 30(2), CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972?
cases.action: The commuted leave becomes half pay leave, and the difference is recovered.
cases.authority: Head of Office / competent authority as fixed by the First Schedule
cases.conclusion: Non-return: recover the difference; waiver only for ill-health retirement or death.
cases.exam_q: In the Ministry of External Affairs, an officer took 40 days of commuted leave for an illness, and on return tendered his resignation without rejoining duty, the resignation being accepted on personal grounds. (Answer: The commuted leave becomes half pay leave, and the difference is recovered.)

cases.title: Case 5: Encashment with pending proceedings
cases.facts: In the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs, a Superintendent retires on superannuation with 190 days of earned leave and 150 days of half pay leave at credit, while disciplinary proceedings for a procedural irregularity are pending against him.
cases.issue: What is the correct position under Rule 39, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972?
cases.action: The cash equivalent may be withheld in whole or in part during the case.
cases.authority: Head of Office / competent authority as fixed by the First Schedule
cases.conclusion: Pending proceedings: withhold part or all of the encashment.
cases.exam_q: In the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs, a Superintendent retires on superannuation with 190 days of earned leave and 150 days of half pay leave at credit, while disciplinary proceedings for a procedural irregularity are pending against him. (Answer: The cash equivalent may be withheld in whole or in part during the case.)

cases.title: Case 6: Death in service with LTC encashment
cases.facts: In the Department of Posts, a Gramin Dak Sevak's supervising officer — a regular Group C official — dies in service with 150 days of earned leave and 90 days of half pay leave at credit, having encashed 30 days of earned leave with LTC three years earlier. The family applies for the cash equivalent.
cases.issue: What is the correct position under Rule 39-A, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972?
cases.action: 270 days — the 30 days already encashed with LTC count against the ceiling.
cases.authority: Head of Office / competent authority as fixed by the First Schedule
cases.conclusion: Death in service: 300 − LTC days = 270 days to the family.
cases.exam_q: In the Department of Posts, a Gramin Dak Sevak's supervising officer — a regular Group C official — dies in service with 150 days of earned leave and 90 days of half pay leave at credit, having encashed 30 days of earned leave with LTC three years earlier. The family applies for the cash equivalent. (Answer: 270 days — the 30 days already encashed with LTC count against the ceiling.)

cases.title: Case 7: CCL spells and pay tranche

cases.authority: Head of Office / competent authority as fixed by the First Schedule

cases.title: Case 8: WRIIL structure
cases.facts: In the Border Security Force, a Deputy Commandant sustains a work related injury and is hospitalised for 45 days, after which the medical board advises a long convalescence. The pay section asks what pay structure applies after discharge from hospital.
cases.issue: What is the correct position under Rule 44(2)(b), CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972?
cases.action: Six months on full pay and allowances, then twenty-four months on full pay.
cases.authority: Head of Office / competent authority as fixed by the First Schedule
cases.conclusion: CAPF officer: 6 months full + 24 months full.
cases.exam_q: In the Border Security Force, a Deputy Commandant sustains a work related injury and is hospitalised for 45 days, after which the medical board advises a long convalescence. The pay section asks what pay structure applies after discharge from hospital. (Answer: Six months on full pay and allowances, then twenty-four months on full pay.)

cases.title: Case 9: Study leave eligibility
cases.facts: In the Ministry of Defence, a Section Officer with four years and eleven months of regular continuous service applies for study leave for a two-year postgraduate programme. He would return four years before superannuation and is willing to execute a bond.
cases.issue: What is the correct position under Rule 50(1)(i), CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972?
cases.action: Premature — five years' continuous service including probation is needed.
cases.authority: Head of Office / competent authority as fixed by the First Schedule
cases.conclusion: Study leave needs 5 years' regular continuous service including probation.
cases.exam_q: In the Ministry of Defence, a Section Officer with four years and eleven months of regular continuous service applies for study leave for a two-year postgraduate programme. He would return four years before superannuation and is willing to execute a bond. (Answer: Premature — five years' continuous service including probation is needed.)

cases.title: Case 10: Study leave — bond execution
cases.facts: In the Indian Audit and Accounts Department, a non-permanent Assistant Accounts Officer is sanctioned study leave for twelve months abroad. The sanctioning authority issues the sanction and the officer leaves the country, the bond being sent for execution after his departure.
cases.issue: What is the correct position under Rule 53(4)(b) and (c), CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972?
cases.action: Defective — the Form 9 bond must precede the leave and go to the Audit Officer.
cases.authority: Head of Office / competent authority as fixed by the First Schedule
cases.conclusion: Non-permanent study leave: Form 9 bond before departure, certificate to the Audit Officer.
cases.exam_q: In the Indian Audit and Accounts Department, a non-permanent Assistant Accounts Officer is sanctioned study leave for twelve months abroad. The sanctioning authority issues the sanction and the officer leaves the country, the bond being sent for execution after his departure. (Answer: Defective — the Form 9 bond must precede the leave and go to the Audit Officer.)

cases.title: Case 11: Study leave refund
cases.facts: In the Ministry of Coal, an officer who returned from study leave eighteen months ago is permitted to retire voluntarily to take up a private-sector appointment. The establishment section has to determine his liability under Rule 63.
cases.issue: What is the correct position under Rule 63(1), CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972?
cases.action: He must refund the salary, allowance, fees, TA and expenses with interest.
cases.authority: Head of Office / competent authority as fixed by the First Schedule
cases.conclusion: Three-year bond period runs from the date of return.
cases.exam_q: In the Ministry of Coal, an officer who returned from study leave eighteen months ago is permitted to retire voluntarily to take up a private-sector appointment. The establishment section has to determine his liability under Rule 63. (Answer: He must refund the salary, allowance, fees, TA and expenses with interest.)

cases.title: Case 12: Holidays with medical-certificate leave
cases.facts: In the Department of Personnel and Training, an Assistant takes 20 days of leave on medical certificate from 12 January to 31 January. Two gazetted holidays fall on 9 and 10 January and two more on 1 and 2 February. The leave section asks how the holidays are to be treated.
cases.issue: What is the correct position under Rule 22(1)(ii), CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972?
cases.action: Both sets of holidays attach automatically and neither is debited.
cases.authority: Head of Office / competent authority as fixed by the First Schedule
cases.conclusion: MC leave: holidays prefix and suffix automatically, undebited.
cases.exam_q: In the Department of Personnel and Training, an Assistant takes 20 days of leave on medical certificate from 12 January to 31 January. Two gazetted holidays fall on 9 and 10 January and two more on 1 and 2 February. The leave section asks how the holidays are to be treated. (Answer: Both sets of holidays attach automatically and neither is debited.)

cases.title: Case 13: Overstay after leave
cases.facts: In the Ministry of Rural Development, a clerk sanctioned 15 days of leave overstays by 35 days, holding 20 days of half pay leave and 120 days of earned leave. He reports for duty on the 36th day with no fresh sanction.
cases.issue: What is the correct position under Rule 25 read with Rule 32, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972?
cases.rules: Rule 25 read with Rule 32, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
cases.action: 20 days of half pay leave and 15 days of extraordinary leave, unpaid.
cases.authority: Head of Office / competent authority as fixed by the First Schedule
cases.conclusion: Overstay: 20 days HPL + 15 days EOL, no leave salary.
cases.exam_q: In the Ministry of Rural Development, a clerk sanctioned 15 days of leave overstays by 35 days, holding 20 days of half pay leave and 120 days of earned leave. He reports for duty on the 36th day with no fresh sanction. (Answer: 20 days of half pay leave and 15 days of extraordinary leave, unpaid.)

cases.title: Case 14: Maximum continuous leave
cases.facts: In the Ministry of Steel, a servant has been on extraordinary leave, interspersed with short spells of duty, for a continuous period of five years and four months. The section seeks to know the consequence under Rule 12.
cases.issue: What is the correct position under Rule 12, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972?
cases.action: He is deemed to have resigned once continuous leave passes five years.
cases.authority: Head of Office / competent authority as fixed by the First Schedule
cases.conclusion: Five years of continuous leave: deemed resignation, President only may extend.
cases.exam_q: In the Ministry of Steel, a servant has been on extraordinary leave, interspersed with short spells of duty, for a continuous period of five years and four months. The section seeks to know the consequence under Rule 12. (Answer: He is deemed to have resigned once continuous leave passes five years.)

cases.title: Case 15: Revocation of leave
cases.facts: In the Ministry of Home Affairs, a servant's earned leave has been sanctioned for 30 days. Two weeks later the department recalls him, and he asks that the recalled period instead be converted into extraordinary leave so that his earned leave balance is preserved.
cases.issue: What is the correct position under Rule 7(2) read with Rule 23(3), CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972?
cases.rules: Rule 7(2) read with Rule 23(3), CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
cases.action: The recall stands; conversion to EOL needs his written request.
cases.authority: Head of Office / competent authority as fixed by the First Schedule
cases.conclusion: Recall is compulsory; the type of leave cannot be changed without the servant's written request.
cases.exam_q: In the Ministry of Home Affairs, a servant's earned leave has been sanctioned for 30 days. Two weeks later the department recalls him, and he asks that the recalled period instead be converted into extraordinary leave so that his earned leave balance is preserved. (Answer: The recall stands; conversion to EOL needs his written request.)

cases.title: Case 16: Provisional sanction
cases.facts: In the Department of Expenditure, the admissibility report for a servant's leave is delayed because his old service book is under reconciliation. The Head of Office decides to sanction the leave provisionally for 75 days so that the servant can travel as planned.
cases.issue: What is the correct position under Rule 16(2), CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972?
cases.action: Defective — the provisional sanction cannot run beyond 60 days.
cases.authority: Head of Office / competent authority as fixed by the First Schedule
cases.conclusion: Provisional sanction: 60 days maximum, modifiable on verification.
cases.exam_q: In the Department of Expenditure, the admissibility report for a servant's leave is delayed because his old service book is under reconciliation. The Head of Office decides to sanction the leave provisionally for 75 days so that the servant can travel as planned. (Answer: Defective — the provisional sanction cannot run beyond 60 days.)

cases.title: Case 17: Applicability — autonomous body
cases.facts: In an autonomous institute under the Ministry of Science and Technology, a staff association argues that the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972 apply to the institute because it is fully funded by the Central Government. The institute's own regulations are silent on leave.
cases.issue: What is the correct position under Rule 2, CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972?
cases.action: The rules reach the institute only so far as its regulations adopt them.
cases.authority: Head of Office / competent authority as fixed by the First Schedule
cases.conclusion: Autonomous body: bound only to the extent of adoption.
cases.exam_q: In an autonomous institute under the Ministry of Science and Technology, a staff association argues that the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972 apply to the institute because it is fully funded by the Central Government. The institute's own regulations are silent on leave. (Answer: The rules reach the institute only so far as its regulations adopt them.)

cases.title: Case 18: Transfer between leave rule-sets
cases.facts: In the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, a servant transfers from a post governed by the Fundamental Rules to a post governed by the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972, carrying 310 days of earned leave at credit. The leave section must decide how much survives the transfer.
cases.issue: What is the correct position under Rule 5 read with Rule 26(1)(b), CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972?
cases.rules: Rule 5 read with Rule 26(1)(b), CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972
cases.action: Only 300 days are carried forward, being the Rule 26 ceiling.
cases.authority: Head of Office / competent authority as fixed by the First Schedule
cases.conclusion: Rule 5: carry forward within the Rule 26 ceiling.
cases.exam_q: In the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, a servant transfers from a post governed by the Fundamental Rules to a post governed by the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972, carrying 310 days of earned leave at credit. The leave section must decide how much survives the transfer. (Answer: Only 300 days are carried forward, being the Rule 26 ceiling.)

cases.title: Case 19: Departmental leave
cases.facts: In the Survey of India, a Class III field assistant in a survey party, other than Division I staff and clerks, is told that his services are not required during the recess. He asks for earned leave instead of departmental leave so that he is paid in full.
cases.issue: What is the correct position under Rule 49(1), (2), (6)(a) and (7), CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972?
cases.action: Departmental leave — 25% of the EL salary plus DA, with no debit.
cases.authority: Head of Office / competent authority as fixed by the First Schedule
cases.conclusion: Departmental leave: 25% + DA, not debited, not duty.
cases.exam_q: In the Survey of India, a Class III field assistant in a survey party, other than Division I staff and clerks, is told that his services are not required during the recess. He asks for earned leave instead of departmental leave so that he is paid in full. (Answer: Departmental leave — 25% of the EL salary plus DA, with no debit.)

cases.title: Case 20: Medical certificate — waiver
cases.facts: In the Ministry of Textiles, a non-Gazetted assistant takes 3 days of leave for a family function and produces no medical certificate. The Head of Office proposes to treat it as leave on medical certificate because a certificate was not produced.

cases.action: Wrong — the certificate is waived up to 3 days and the leave is not MC leave.

cases.conclusion: Up to 3 days: certificate waived, and the leave is not MC leave.

amendments.subject: Bringing the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972 into force
amendments.summary: Principal instrument; Rule 1(2) fixes commencement at 1 June 1972.

amendments.subject: Commuted leave recast; clauses (b), (c) and (e) of Rule 30(1) deleted
amendments.summary: The double-debit rule in Rule 30(1)(d) is the operative limb today.

amendments.subject: Rule 23(1) and (2) deleted; EOL limits in Rule 32(2) recast; Rule 12 and Rule 19 amendments
amendments.summary: Recall to duty survives only as Rule 23(3).

amendments.subject: Holidays prefix and suffix automatically to medical-certificate leave
amendments.summary: The automatic concession is the point examiners test.

amendments.subject: Rules 35, 36 and 37 deleted
amendments.summary: The gap between Rule 34 and Rule 38 is real, not a printing error.

amendments.subject: Leave not due extended to 360 days, including temporary servants with TB, leprosy, cancer or mental illness
amendments.summary: The 360-day lifetime ceiling and the 31(1-A) temporary-servant route come from here.

amendments.subject: EL accumulation 240 to 300 days; carry-over buffer 225 to 285; the 120-day figure becomes 150
amendments.summary: Every book printed before this date is wrong on both numbers.

amendments.subject: LPR earned leave raised from 240 to 300 days
amendments.summary: Rule 39(2) encashment ceiling follows the same figure.

amendments.subject: Maternity leave raised from 135 to 180 days; child care leave introduced
amendments.summary: The 730-day CCL entitlement dates from this notification.

amendments.subject: Child adoption leave of 180 days
amendments.summary: Female servant; child below one year; not debited to the leave account.

amendments.subject: Encashment of EL and HPL on retirement, 300-day ceiling, no commutation to top up EL
amendments.summary: Suo motu order; HRA excluded from the base.

amendments.subject: EL encashment with LTC — 10 days an occasion, 60 a career, 30-day floor, 2% interest on default
amendments.summary: The 2% over-PF interest is the enforcement mechanism.

amendments.subject: Maximum continuous leave of five years and deemed resignation beyond it
amendments.summary: Only the President may extend the period.

amendments.subject: Special leave of 90 days for an inquiry into sexual harassment; rule number substituted
amendments.summary: Granted on the recommendation of the Internal or Local Committee.

amendments.subject: Form 3-A disability certificate: four additional authorities; no Head of Office reference
amendments.summary: The 12-month limb in Rule 20 comes with this amendment.

amendments.subject: 7th CPC: WRIIL substituted; Rules 45 and 46 omitted; Rule 28 and 29 credits restated
amendments.summary: Special disability leave and hospital leave cease to exist.

amendments.subject: WRIIL pay structure clarified — 6 + 12 civil, 6 + 24 CAPF officers, no limit below officer rank; CCL single-parent clarification
amendments.summary: No EL or HPL is credited during WRIIL.

amendments.subject: Organ donation special casual leave raised from 30 to 42 days
amendments.summary: Non-statutory: it is an O.M., not a rule.

core.fact: Earned leave is credited 15 days per half-year, in advance, on 1 January and 1 July.
EL may accumulate up to 300 days.
EL granted at a time in India is capped at 180 days, even from a 300-day balance.
For leave spent outside the listed countries, the at-a-time cap rises to 300 days.
EL is earned at 2 1/2 days per completed calendar month.
Half pay leave is credited 10 days per half-year — 20 days a year.
HPL is earned at 5/3 days per completed month.
HPL has no accumulation ceiling.
Penalty in the EL account for EOL: one-tenth of the period, limited to 15 days.
Penalty in the HPL account: one-eighteenth of the period, limited to 10 days.
One day of commuted leave debits two days of HPL.
Commuted leave for study is capped at 180 days.
Leave not due ceiling: 360 days in the entire service.
Extraordinary leave has no ceiling, but five years of continuous absence ends the service.
Unavailed joining time credited to EL is capped at 15 days, and EL plus joining time may not exceed 300.
The 285-day buffer: above 285 at half-year end, the 15-day credit is held apart.
Retirement encashment: EL plus HPL, capped at 300 days.
Death in service: 300 days to the family, less LTC encashment already taken.
PSU absorption: EL only, capped at 300 days.
LTC encashment: 10 days an occasion, 60 a career, minimum balance 30 days.
LPR: EL up to 300 days plus HPL, up to the date of retirement.
A foreign employer may grant EL of not more than 120 days at a time.
Maternity leave: 180 days; miscarriage or abortion: 45 days.
Paternity leave: 15 days, within a window from 15 days before to six months after delivery.
Paternity leave on adoption: 15 days.
Child adoption leave: 180 days, female servant, child below one year.
Child care leave: 730 days in the entire service, for the two eldest surviving children.
CCL spells: six a year for a single female parent, three for others; 5 days minimum, 120 days maximum in a spell.
CCL pay: 100% for the first 365 days, 80% for the next 365.
Sexual harassment leave: 90 days.
WRIIL beyond hospitalisation: 6 months full pay plus 12 months half pay.
WRIIL for CAPF officers: 6 months full plus 24 months full; below officer rank: no limit.
No EL or HPL is credited during WRIIL.
Study leave ceiling: 24 months, ordinarily 12 at a time; 36 months for CHS.
Study leave needs 5 years' service including probation and a bond of 3 years (5 for CHS).
Study leave plus other leave: total absence of 28 months, or 36 for a Ph.D.
Departmental leave salary: 25% of EL salary plus DA.
Holidays may be prefixed or suffixed to leave and are not debited.
Leave is not a matter of right, but a refusal should still be by written order.
Deleted or omitted: Rules 18, 23(1)-(2), 30(1)(b)(c)(e), 32(2)(c), 35-37, 45, 46, and 58-59 omitted.

forms_note: Rule 3(h) of the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972 defines a 'Form' as a Form appended to the Second Schedule. That is the only appended series these rules have: there is no separate Formats series, and no instrument in the rules is described as a Format. The 11 Forms in the 'forms' key are therefore the complete set. This differs from the CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021, where rule 3 defines a Form (clause (k)) and a Format (clause (l)) as two distinct appended series.
